account:
Today I have been keeping my appointments and asking for local news. I still have a feeling that something may be happening without my knowledge, but I have no solid evidence of a secret undertaking or wrongdoing. My notes mention a builder's public request that I intended to investigate; I do not remember its details, and later I heard the builder shouting without making out the words. A towns-person told me the baker was carrying a sack of bread near the plaza. That could simply be ordinary bakery business; I have seen nothing establishing another purpose.

The neighbour personally confirmed tea today at fifteen hundred at the cottage at (16, -60, 105), beside the east ferry landing. The secretary had been trying to verify the host, even asking dockside workers, who reportedly had no information. I supplied the direct confirmation and said further verification was unnecessary. I do not know of any purpose for this tea beyond the neighbour's invitation.

The thirteen-hundred town-accounts appointment has produced no papers. The secretary said no particular account issues had been brought forward, then asked me where the accounts are kept. I do not know. This looks like an administrative gap, not proof of misconduct. The secretary also reported that Freight was coordinating warehouse supplies, which may be routine work.

The innkeeper requested a meeting tomorrow at eighteen in the great hall about an unspecified inn matter. There has been repeated confusion about whether I accepted: my earlier reply was heard by the secretary but not the innkeeper. I have now explicitly approved it and asked the secretary to record it as confirmed and notify him. I saw the secretary put a written book into the appointments chest, but have not read it to verify the entry. I do not yet know what the inn matter concerns. My next commitments are today's tea at fifteen hundred and office at sixteen-thirty.
